problem: "affected to be" (made a show of being) softened to "claimed to be"; "named President" rendered "elected President", which asserts a mode of choice the source does not state.
replacement: The party that wished to limit the power of the people tried to apply its doctrines especially to the Constitution of the Union, and from this it took its name of Federal. The other party, which made a show of being more exclusively attached to the cause of liberty, took the name of Republican. America is a land of democracy, and the Federalists were always in a minority. But they counted on their side almost all the great men whom the War of Independence had brought forward, and their moral influence was very considerable. Circumstances also favored their cause. The collapse of the Confederation had given the people a dread of anarchy, and the Federalists did not fail to profit from this passing mood of the multitude. For ten or twelve years they were at the head of affairs, and they were able to apply some, though not all, of their principles, for the opposing current was growing too violent day by day to be checked or resisted. In 1801 the Republicans took control of the government. Thomas Jefferson was chosen President, and he increased the influence of their party by the weight of his fame, the greatness of his talents, and the immense extent of his popularity.
